Hey /v/gamedev! I've been working on a game for a few weeks now and I've been considering starting a devlog, half for exposure, half for motivation, half for communication with followers, and half for inaccurate percentages.

I have experience with web development, and could have a blog up in no time, but it just seems like a waste to do that when there's so many options to host a blog. I've been eyeing tumblr, though I know the community can be a bit... interesting, I've also been considering wordpress, which I also have experience with.

What do you guys think? Tumblr, wordpress, custom site, or other?
Thinking about starting a devlog/blog, any advice on hosting, or just advice in general?

I spend a bit of time on Tumblr, I find games with good art do fairly well there. Likes and reblogs help with motivation and people can share your game easily as well. If you're making a blog there, people generally prefer media posts (gifs and screenshots).

Unfortunately, Tumblr doesn't really have an easy way to discuss things with others (no real back-and-forth commenting system). If you want to get real feedback on what you're doing then I'd recommend the TIGForums. I'd recommend doing that even if you have a blog elsewhere, good place to network naturally, see other games, interact with devs etc. It's not really for getting consumers (although you will pick up fans etc.)

Personally I wouldn't do a blog that's on it's own website/wordpress. There's nothing wrong with it per se, but starting out it makes more sense to have a dev blog that is somewhere that has a somewhat high visibility to start with. When you gather your own following then having a socially separated website makes sense.

You should have a complimentary Twitter account as well if you don't have one already.

GitHub pages are great: they're free and you can easily use your own domain name. To host a blog on GitHub pages, you use a Static Site Generator; pick one of the more popular ones and you'll be fine. You can embed Disqus comment blocks in each of your blog pages and it'll just work.

I'd stay away from Tumblr, but not just for the community. Modifying your blog's CSS is a nightmare and I've never found an easy way to embed properly formatted code.
